title: Health, the body and the pharmacy
goal: By the end of this lesson you can name the main parts of the body, say where it hurts and what symptoms you have, and get help at a pharmacy, a CLSC or a clinic in Quebec.

body: Learn body parts with their article, because the article changes in the key expression *avoir mal à*: *la tête*, *le dos*, *le ventre*, *la gorge*, *les yeux*.

Watch the irregular plurals: *un œil* → *des yeux*, *le genou* → *les genoux*. And note that French uses the definite article with body parts where English uses *my*: *Je me lave les mains* (I wash my hands), *Il s'est cassé le bras* (He broke his arm).

learn.h: Saying where it hurts: avoir mal à
body: To say something hurts, use *avoir mal à* + body part. The *à* contracts with the article like always: *à + le* = *au*, *à + les* = *aux*, but *à la* and *à l'* stay.
*J'ai mal à la tête* (I have a headache), *J'ai mal au dos* (my back hurts), *J'ai mal aux dents* (I have a toothache), *J'ai mal à l'oreille* (I have an earache).
To ask: *Où avez-vous mal?* / *Tu as mal où?* (Where does it hurt?). *Ça fait mal* means 'it hurts' in general, and *Ça me fait mal ici* means 'it hurts here'.
learn.tip: au, à la, à l', aux: the same contractions you already use with places (au dépanneur, à la pharmacie).

body: Many symptoms use *avoir*: *avoir de la fièvre* (to have a fever), *avoir le rhume* (to have a cold), *avoir la grippe* (to have the flu), *avoir la toux* or *tousser* (to cough), *avoir le nez qui coule* (to have a runny nose).
Others use *être*: *être malade* (to be sick), *être enrhumé(e)* (to have a cold), *être fatigué(e)*, *être enceinte* (to be pregnant).
Use the passé composé for what happened: *Je me suis coupé le doigt* (I cut my finger), *Elle s'est fait mal au genou* (She hurt her knee), *Il est tombé* (He fell).
In Quebec the pharmacist (*le pharmacien*, *la pharmacienne*) can give a lot of advice and even treat some minor problems, so the pharmacy is often the first stop.

Useful phrases: *Avez-vous quelque chose pour la toux?* (Do you have something for a cough?), *Est-ce que j'ai besoin d'une ordonnance?* (Do I need a prescription?), *Combien de fois par jour?* (How many times a day?), *Je suis allergique à la pénicilline* (I'm allergic to penicillin).
Medicine words: *le médicament* (medication), *le comprimé* (tablet), *le sirop* (syrup), *la pommade* or *la crème* (ointment), *le pansement* (bandage).

learn.h: The Quebec health system in French
body: Your health card is officially *la carte d'assurance maladie*, issued by the RAMQ, but everyone calls it *la carte soleil* because of the old sun logo.

A *CLSC* (centre local de services communautaires) is a local public health centre for vaccines, nurses, blood tests and social services. For non-urgent advice you can call *Info-Santé 811*. For an emergency, go to *l'urgence* (the ER) or call *le 911*.
In Quebec, *avoir mal au cœur* does not mean your heart hurts: it means you feel nauseous. This is also the meaning in France. To say your heart or chest hurts, say *J'ai mal à la poitrine*.
learn.tip: Mal au cœur = nausea. Mal à la poitrine = chest pain (go to the ER!).

examples.en: Take two tablets three times a day.
examples.note: imperative with vous, typical pharmacist instruction

examples.note: arachides is the usual word on Canadian labels; cacahuètes in France

quebec.intro: Quebec health vocabulary includes a few local names: the health card is 'la carte soleil', the local public clinic is the CLSC, and 'avoir mal au cœur' means nausea, not heart pain.

items.note: Everyday name, from the old sun logo of the RAMQ card
Also used in France; never means heart pain
Prescription is very common in Quebec speech; ordonnance is the official word
Both are correct; avoir le rhume is the usual Quebec phrasing
Quebec uses the singular l'urgence; France says les urgences
Informal; chu = je suis in fast speech

drills.q: How do you say 'My back hurts'?
In Quebec, 'J'ai mal au cœur' means…
drills.why: Avoir mal au cœur = to feel sick to your stomach.

drills.q: What is the plural of 'un œil'?
drills.why: Œil has an irregular plural: yeux.

drills.q: Where would you go in Quebec for a vaccine or a blood test without an emergency?
drills.why: The CLSC is the local public health centre.
Before a vowel, à + l' stays separate.
French uses the definite article with body parts after a pronominal verb.

dialogue.fr: Bonjour, est-ce que je peux vous aider?
Oui, j'ai mal à la gorge et je tousse depuis trois jours.
dialogue.en: Yes, I have a sore throat and I've been coughing for three days.

dialogue.fr: Est-ce que vous avez de la fièvre?
Non, mais je suis très fatiguée et j'ai le nez qui coule.
dialogue.en: No, but I'm very tired and I have a runny nose.

dialogue.fr: C'est probablement un rhume. Je vous conseille ce sirop.
dialogue.en: It's probably a cold. I recommend this syrup.

dialogue.fr: Est-ce que j'ai besoin d'une prescription?
Non, c'est sans ordonnance. Prenez-en une cuillère trois fois par jour.
dialogue.en: No, it's over the counter. Take one spoonful three times a day.

dialogue.fr: Parfait. Et si ça ne va pas mieux?
dialogue.en: Perfect. And if it doesn't get better?

dialogue.fr: Appelez Info-Santé au 811 ou allez au CLSC.
dialogue.en: Call Info-Santé at 811 or go to the CLSC.
Thanks a lot, have a nice day!

speak.prompt: You have a headache and a sore throat. Tell the pharmacist and ask for something.
speak.model: Bonjour, j'ai mal à la tête et mal à la gorge. Avez-vous quelque chose pour ça?

speak.prompt: Say three body parts that hurt after a long day of moving boxes.
speak.model: J'ai mal au dos, j'ai mal aux bras et j'ai mal aux genoux.

speak.prompt: Explain that you feel nauseous, the Quebec way, and that you have a fever.
speak.model: J'ai mal au cœur et j'ai de la fièvre depuis hier soir.

speak.prompt: Ask the pharmacist how many times a day to take the medication and whether you need a prescription.
speak.model: Combien de fois par jour est-ce que je dois le prendre? Et est-ce que j'ai besoin d'une ordonnance?

write.prompt: Write a short message (5–6 sentences) to your boss explaining that you are sick today: your symptoms, since when, and what you are going to do.
write.model: Bonjour Julie, je suis malade aujourd'hui. J'ai de la fièvre et j'ai mal à la gorge depuis hier soir. J'ai aussi mal à la tête et je tousse beaucoup. Je vais aller à la pharmacie ce matin. Si ça ne va pas mieux, je vais appeler le 811. Je pense revenir au travail jeudi. Merci et bonne journée!

quiz.q: What does 'la carte soleil' refer to?
quiz.why: It's the everyday name for the RAMQ health insurance card.

quiz.q: Which number gives non-urgent health advice in Quebec?
How do you say 'He broke his arm'?
quiz.why: Pronominal verb + definite article; pronominal verbs use être.
Un comprimé = a pill or tablet.

quiz.q: To talk about chest pain, you say…
quiz.why: Mal au cœur means nausea; chest pain is mal à la poitrine.

quiz.q: Which phrase means 'over the counter' (no prescription needed)?
